title: Protect America's Workforce Act
official_title: To nullify the Executive Order relating to Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Jared Golden (D-ME) with 226 cosponsors — one of the largest cosponsor blocs in the batch. The House-passed measure has moved to the Senate per the latest recorded action.
summary: Section 2 declares the March 27, 2025 Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" of no force or effect and bars any federal funds from being obligated or expended to carry it out. Section 3 preserves any collective bargaining agreement in effect as of March 26, 2025 between an executive branch federal agency and an exclusive representative of federal employees through the stated term of that agreement.
brief: Nullifies the March 27, 2025 executive order excluding federal agencies from federal labor-management relations programs and preserves collective bargaining agreements that were in effect the day before the order.

top_lines.headline: Executive Order Nullified
subs: Applies to the Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" issued March 27, 2025
The order "shall have no force or effect"
No federal funds may be obligated or expended to carry it out

top_lines.headline: Existing CBAs Preserved
subs: Covers collective bargaining agreements in effect as of March 26, 2025
Agreements between executive branch federal agencies and exclusive representatives of federal employees
They have full force and effect through the stated term of the applicable agreement

items.main: Names the Act the "Protect America's Workforce Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Nullification of Executive Order Relating to Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs

items.main: The March 27, 2025 Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" is declared to have no force or effect, and no federal funds may be obligated or expended to carry it out.
items.detail: The section identifies the order by title and issuance date but does not list which specific agencies or bargaining units it addressed.

items.main: Any collective bargaining agreement in effect as of March 26, 2025 between any executive branch federal agency and any labor organization that is an exclusive representative of federal employees has full force and effect through the stated term of the applicable agreement.
items.detail: The section fixes eligibility to the day before the executive order but does not distinguish among agencies or bargaining units.

gaps: The bill does not restate which agencies or units the March 27, 2025 executive order covered; the scope of what is being nullified is not described in the Act itself.
The bill does not address collective bargaining agreements negotiated after March 26, 2025 or renewals during the covered agreements' stated terms.
The bill does not provide a remedy or enforcement mechanism for actions taken between March 27, 2025 and enactment.
The bill does not set an effective date beyond the general rule for enactment.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Comer
featured_quotes.text: That was a long minute for the leader of the Democratic Party to advocate for more work-from-home policies for our Federal employees. I think the American people have spoken loud and clear. They support our Federal employees, like the Republican Party, but we expect them to show up for work, not get paid to be home and not be accessible by phone or by computer or by email. That is what we heard from the leader of the Democratic Party.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Cloud
featured_quotes.text: The proposed legislation is designed to nullify President Trump's lawful executive order to exclude agencies with national security missions from collective bargaining agreements. Article II of the Constitution is crystal clear: The executive power is invested in the President of the United States. Let me repeat: All authority in the executive branch flows from the people to the duly elected executive.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Fitzpatrick
featured_quotes.text: This legislation reaffirms a core principle: A government that serves the people must also respect the rights of those who serve within it. Federal employees work tirelessly every day, often behind the scenes. They process Social Security benefits, safeguard our food and water, care for our veterans, and respond whenever a disaster strikes. Their work is essential, and its impact reaches every community across this Nation.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Biggs
featured_quotes.text: This bill would nullify President Trump's Executive Order No. 14251, which rightly excluded 40 national security agencies from collective bargaining. Agencies like FEMA, the Coast Guard, the CDC, and the VA cannot afford to be paralyzed by union red tape when lives are on the line. I want to emphasize that this is going to nullify an executive order. It is going to attack his agenda, the America First agenda, that he was overwhelmingly elected to enact. These unions are not neutral actors.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Norcross
featured_quotes.text: Earlier this year, President Trump launched one of the largest attacks on labor in the history of the United States, on the working people who voted to join a union and have a voice. President Trump suggests that this is a problem of national security. Quite frankly, it has not been. They cited that there would be strikes. There hasn't been, and it is illegal to strike. In fact, we are looking for workers to help build our military at the very time that the President is trying to beat down those workers. This is where the real problem is.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Krishnamoorthi
featured_quotes.text: This bipartisan bill reverses an illegal executive order that stripped collective bargaining rights from roughly 67 percent of the Federal workforce, so more than two-thirds of the Federal workforce. Removing their limited bargaining rights does not improve efficiency. It threatens the integrity of our civil service. These rights exist for one essential reason: to shield Federal employees from political pressure so that they serve the American people, not the agenda of any one President or political party.

added: Preservation of collective bargaining agreements in effect between executive branch federal agencies and exclusive representatives as of March 26, 2025, through their stated terms
removed: Force and effect of the Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" issued March 27, 2025, together with any federal funding to carry it out
